candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

'And from thence I went to another place to the west of the ends of the earth. And I saw a burning fire which ran without resting, and paused not from its course day or night but ran regularly' — Enoch beholds the perpetual fire of the divine judicial process. The 'without resting' (Geez 'enza i-yenuh) establishes the perpetuity of divine judgment: the fire of judgment is not episodic but ongoing, constantly burning even when not visibly applied. This grounds the Tewahedo theological reading that divine justice is not occasional intervention but continuous operation — what humans experience as discrete acts of judgment are visible occasions of a permanently-burning process.
